about.title: About me
about.subtitle: Qianli Gu · a note from the author
about.p1: I’ve spent a decade building financial products—mainly front-end, with back-end when needed—across account opening, funding, market data, trading, and risk. Over time one thing became clear: retail investors face an uneven field. On the other side are institutions and quant teams with deeper research, execution, systems, and discipline; individuals are often short on information, tools, and time. I paid tuition myself: my worst drawdown was over 65%, and I still clung to that position, unwilling to admit the mistake and get out. Only afterward did it sink in—without timely review, mistakes repeat; without rules you can actually follow, emotion takes the next order. I built Qianli Gu first as personal learning and engineering practice, and as a toolkit I can use again and again. If you’ve taken similar detours, you’re welcome to review with a cooler head here too.
about.p2: If you can introduce me to Futu or Longbridge business teams, I’d love to explore a deeper partnership.
about.p3: If you can spare some “ammo” (budget), help top up API tokens — they’ll go toward more AI finance features.
about.p4: Thanks to everyone who stops by.
about.qrHint: Scan to tip, or email for collaboration.
about.mainlandNotice: Note for friends in mainland China: investing in overseas stocks or BTC is currently illegal. This site is for learning only — please follow local laws.
about.platformBody: The idea behind Qianli Gu is simple: no stock tips, no “buy this / sell that” verdicts. We use AI and rules to connect research, a calmer pause before you order, and post-trade review—so fear and greed have less room to steer the next decision. Market data and content are for learning only, not investment advice.
about.lead: Qianli Gu is a multi-market quote and research tool for individual investors: A-shares, Hong Kong, US and crypto in one interface — screen, research, paper-trade, review. One person builds and maintains it. It does not sell data, does not recommend stocks, and does not decide for you.
about.originP2: When I went back through every losing trade, the problem was rarely that I did not know something. It sat in four places: the information arrived too late, the judgement had no standard, the order carried emotion, and nothing was written down afterwards. Those four feed each other — no record means no review, no review means no standard, no standard leaves only emotion, and emotion chases more news.
about.originP3: So I did not build a product that tells you what to buy. I built tools that fix the process: compress information into something readable, write the thesis down before the order, keep the result on file, compare next time. The asymmetry does not disappear — but your own mistakes become reproducible, and therefore fixable.
about.principlesLead: These decide what gets built and what does not. Anything that encourages overtrading, or lets uncertainty pass for certainty, is out.
about.principle1Title: It does not decide for you
about.principle1Body: AI is for reading, not predicting. It condenses filings, news and unusual moves into points and raises the questions worth asking — but it gives no buy or sell call, because it does not know either.
about.principle2Body: Every paper trade can carry a written reason. Comparing what you thought then with what actually happened beats any extra indicator.
about.principle3Body: Where the data came from, how delayed it is, whether it degraded, whether it arrived at all — all of it is on screen. I would rather show “no data” than guess a number.
about.principle4Body: Market credentials are yours (BYOK) and stored encrypted with AES-256-GCM. The platform never trades for you, never exports your positions, and never uses your credentials to serve anyone else.
about.boundary1: Not a stock-tipping service or a licensed adviser: there are no buy signals and no return promises here.
about.boundary2: Not a live trading channel. Every order happens inside a paper account; no broker trading API is connected.
about.boundary3: Not an authoritative source of real-time quotes. Free or BYOK feeds have delays and gaps — for decisions that matter, trust your broker terminal.
about.boundary4: Not a content farm. The writing and tools are by-products of my own use. Fewer, not trendier.
about.roadmap1Body: Fold the deployment into a single docker compose: bring your own credentials, run it on your own machine, keep the data at home.
about.roadmap2Body: Move from “why did this trade lose” to “why do I always lose on this kind of trade” — rules instead of memory.
about.roadmap3Body: Features such as candle forecasting are labelled explicitly as shape demos, never as trading signals.
about.quote: No record, no review. No review, and the same mistake simply repeats.
about.originP4: Start with the asymmetry itself. Institutions have analysts covering sectors, systems that execute for them, and risk controls that force a stop; an individual has fragmented time and a phone. That is not a difference in effort, it is a difference in structure — and trying to be faster and more accurate than the other side from a structurally weaker position is, most of the time, a losing game.
about.originP5: Then what a tool can change. It cannot make information symmetric, but it can make the process symmetric: whatever the account size, the thesis, the position cap and the outcome can all live in the same place. On that layer, the gap between an individual and an institution can actually be closed.
about.originP6: And finally, why I started from review. Going through my trade confirmations, the biggest losses were the ones where I could no longer explain, afterwards, why I had bought; the gains usually came from trades where I had written down in advance what would make me sell. So the record became the foundation of the product rather than a feature on top.

advancedQuotes.statusBody: q-stock currently runs on basic quotes (typically Level-1: last, change, volume) for learning and demo watching. Depth books, tick detail, and lower-latency feeds require a separate enablement and are off by default.
advancedQuotes.what1: Beyond a single last price, they usually include multi-level bid/ask depth, broker queues, or trade-by-trade detail.
advancedQuotes.what2: Update rates and latency are closer to exchange or broker pro terminals—useful for reading short-term supply and demand.
advancedQuotes.what3: Access is licensed by exchanges/brokers and often billed by market, product, and concurrent devices.
advancedQuotes.what4: US, HK, and A-share advanced products differ in name and fields; confirm coverage per market.
advancedQuotes.why1: See multi-level liquidity and how orders are taken—not just one last print.
advancedQuotes.why2: Watch large prints and whether support/resistance is absorbed or swept.
advancedQuotes.why3: Depth-aware strategies, backtests, or teaching demos need finer microstructure than Level-1.
advancedQuotes.why4: In pro trading and risk workflows, latency and depth affect timing judgment (still subject to local law; not investment advice).
advancedQuotes.basic1: Last, change %, volume and similar overview fields
advancedQuotes.basic2: Fits learning, watchlists, and everyday scanning
advancedQuotes.basic3: Limited or no depth / tick detail
advancedQuotes.advanced1: Multi-level book and richer trade detail
advancedQuotes.advanced2: Push experience closer to pro terminals
advancedQuotes.buyBody: Advanced quotes need exchange/broker licensing; fees and coverage vary. Email your target markets (US/HK/CN), use case (study vs deploy demo), and device count—we will assess options and a quote.
advancedQuotes.footnote: This site does not open brokerage accounts, take deposits, or match orders. Quotes and tools are for learning only—follow local law and the disclaimer.

strategies.title: Rule lab
strategies.subtitle: Educational rule templates, paper tags, and single-symbol replay.
strategies.disclaimer: Rule replay uses historical daily closes and simplified fills. It does not predict future results and is not investment advice.
strategies.loginHint: Sign in to copy templates and save strategies.

strategies.name: Name
strategies.symbolPlaceholder: Search ticker or name, e.g. AAPL
strategies.introBody: The Rule Lab is for write → replay → review the path — not tips or promised returns. Finish one loop before tweaking for “better” curves.
strategies.introStep1: Pick a clear template (MA cross, DCA) and Copy it into My strategies.
strategies.introStep2: Edit key numbers in Blocks (MA length, stop %, hold bars), then Save.
strategies.introStep3: Set symbol + range, queue a replay; note return, drawdown, and trade count.
strategies.introStep4: Optional: compare, tiny param grid, or a symbol basket — without treating the best past param as destiny.
strategies.introNote: Replay ≠ future performance. If triggers are too frequent or drawdowns feel unbearable, change the rule or size down — don’t chase the curve.
strategies.emptyHistory: No replays yet. Open a strategy and queue a rule replay.
